---
title: "Courses"
description: "Hands-on classes with All of Us data, taught with R and Python notebooks in the Researcher Workbench 2.0"
---

Each course is a **series of classes**. Every class is a Jupyter notebook you run in your own *All of Us* workspace, plus a page on this site with the overview, class plan, concepts, step-by-step Workbench instructions, and the results we found when we ran it.

All the series share **one research question**, type 2 diabetes, and one cohort definition, so what you learn in one carries over to the next.

| Series | Classes | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [**Core: Cohorts to Analysis**](core/index.qmd) | 1.1–3.4: build a cohort with SQL; clean, reshape, and join; Table One, regression, survival analysis | Notebooks and companion pages ready |
| [**Omics**](omics/index.qmd) | 4.1–4.7: genomes, GWAS with PLINK and Hail, PheWAS, RNA-seq, proteomics | Notebooks and companion pages ready |
| [**Surveys**](surveys/index.qmd) | 5.1–5.3: survey structure, family history and lifestyle, social factors | 5.1 ready; 5.2 and 5.3 in progress |
| **Wearables** | 6.1–6.3: Fitbit basics, steps, sleep and heart rate | Planned |

## How a class works

1. **Before class:** set up your workspace and app once (see [Get Started](../get-started/about.qmd) and [Your Workspace](../workspace/workspaces.qmd)), and run **0.0 setup**.
2. **In class:** the instructor walks through the notebook. At each **✋ Try It Out** you run the next cells or an exercise yourself.
3. **After class:** stop your app, so it stops costing money.

::: {.callout-note}
## The notebooks and this site work together

The **notebooks** are self-contained: you can work through them on your own. This **site** adds what a notebook can't do well: the class plan, diagrams, Workbench walk-throughs, "Try It Out" pauses, our results to compare with, and instructor notes.
:::

## Acknowledgment and data availability

We gratefully acknowledge *All of Us* participants for their contributions, without whom this research would not have been possible. We also thank the National Institutes of Health's *All of Us* Research Program for making available the participant data examined in these materials.

The course results on this site used data from the *All of Us* Research Program's **Controlled Tier Dataset v9** (and **v8** on the Data Explorer page), available to authorized users on the **Researcher Workbench**. All results shown are summary statistics; no participant-level data, and no counts from 1 to 20, are published, in line with the *All of Us* [Data and Statistics Dissemination Policy](https://support.researchallofus.org/hc/en-us/articles/22346276580372-Data-and-Statistics-Dissemination-Policy).
